questions.question: When sitting on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to hold up your body.
Sit at an angle so your arms can support your weight.
Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so you can use your arms to control the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sit with good posture so your arms can control the motorcycle. Your arms should not be used to hold up your body or support your weight.

questions.question: How is the accelerator controlled?
questions.explanation: The accelerator is on the right handgrip and is controlled with your right hand.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Look over their shoulder when taking a turn or curve.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over their shoulder when taking a turn or curve.
questions.explanation: Ask your passenger to look over your shoulder in the direction of any turn or curve. This helps you and the bike lean the right way.

questions.question: Footrests:

options.text: May be shared by the driver and passenger
Are required for the driver and passenger

questions.correctAnswerText: Are required for the driver and passenger
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for balance. The motorcycle must have footrests for both the driver and passenger. This prevents your passenger from falling off and pulling you off too.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means right turns are not allowed.

questions.question: To reduce the chances of a collision, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Stare straight in front of their motorcycle.
Be unwilling to move to avoid a potential hazard.
Scan their path of travel, looking at least 10 to 15 seconds ahead of their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan their path of travel, looking at least 10 to 15 seconds ahead of their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Always scan the road at least 10 to 15 seconds ahead of you. This gives you time to react to hazards before you reach them.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a method used to maintain control of a motorcycle in a turn?
questions.explanation: To stay in control during a turn, slow down before you turn. Look through the turn in the direction you want to go. Lean the bike in the right direction and roll on the throttle through the turn to keep the suspension stable.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a potentially slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Slippery surfaces include wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel roads; lane markings; and metal covers like steel plates.

questions.question: To improve your chances of being seen, you should:

options.text: Use your headlight only at night or when conditions reduce visibility.
Add an orange tint to your headlight.

questions.explanation: Riding with your headlight on at all times is the best way to help others see your motorcycle.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.explanation: Get into the habit of using both the front and rear brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Motorcyclists are usually easiest to see when riding in which lane position?
questions.explanation: The center lane position is best when following a car. This position puts the motorcycle in the driver's rearview mirror where they can see it. Be ready to change positions if traffic or conditions require it.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's stopping power. Use both the front and rear brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: When can motorcycles pass on the right?

options.text: If there is at least eight feet of unobstructed pavement.
By riding on the shoulder of the road.
By riding on the grass, if it is level.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is at least eight feet of unobstructed pavement.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists may pass on the right only if there is unobstructed pavement at least eight feet wide to the right of the vehicle being passed. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: If carrying a package while riding a motorcycle, you:

options.text: May use one hand to steer while using the other hand to hold the package.
Need to keep both hands on the handlebars.
Can rest the package in front of you and occasionally use your hands to hold the package.

questions.correctAnswerText: Need to keep both hands on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: You cannot carry anything that keeps your hands off the handlebars. You must keep both hands on the handlebars at all times while riding.

questions.question: When traveling in a group, riders should generally be:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. It keeps the group together while giving each rider enough space. Use single-file formation when turning, taking curves, entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to weave while riding over uneven metal bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Downshift immediately to a lower gear.
Proceed in a zigzag pattern until you cross the bridge.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle weaves over uneven bridge gratings, stay calm and steer straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than the weaving itself.

questions.question: Alcohol reaches the brain ________ being consumed.
questions.explanation: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes of being consumed and immediately affects your riding ability. Riding while under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If you approach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to signal that the other vehicle should proceed.
You should continue through the intersection and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left should yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When riding in a group on a straight road, motorcyclists should:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps the group close while giving each rider enough space. Switch to single-file when turning, riding in curves, or entering or leaving a roadway.

questions.question: Which factor does not significantly affect your blood alcohol content (BAC)?
questions.explanation: Important factors that affect BAC include the amount of alcohol consumed, how fast it was consumed, and body weight. Age does not play a major role in determining BAC.

questions.question: When should you use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch?

options.text: The throttle is stuck and you cannot move it.
You start to lose control in a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: The throttle is stuck and you cannot move it.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch right away. This stops power to the rear wheel so you can safely leave the road and stop.

questions.question: When should riders use their headlights?
questions.explanation: Use your headlight at all times. Other drivers see your headlight before they see your motorcycle. South Carolina law requires all motorcycles to have headlights on whenever the motorcycle is being used.

questions.question: When riding ________, you are most likely to have a conflict with other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most conflicts happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. When you approach an intersection, position your motorcycle so other drivers can see you clearly.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle?

options.text: Maintain eye contact with other drivers.

questions.explanation: Using your headlight is the best way to help other drivers see your motorcycle. Always check that your headlight works before you start your trip.

questions.question: When making a U-turn, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
Use the front brake to keep the motorcycle stable.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the front brake because it could tip the bike over.
questions.explanation: Do not use the front brake during a U-turn because it can tip the bike over. Instead, use the rear brake to control your speed during the U-turn.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Avoid sudden moves because they could cause a skid.
Ride on the shoulder to stay out of traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake does not work well on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves because they could cause a skid.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, any sudden change in speed or direction can cause a skid. Move smoothly when you speed up, shift gears, turn, or brake.

questions.question: What should you do if you need to shift gears while turning?

options.text: Shifting while turning is better than shifting before the turn.
Shifting in a turn is the best way to control your speed.

questions.explanation: It is best to change gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden change in power to the rear wheel can cause a skid.

questions.question: In dangerous areas, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Hold the clutch and both brake levers ready to reduce reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the clutch and both brake levers ready to reduce reaction time.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping centers, schools, or construction zones, slow down. Keep your hands ready on the clutch and both brake levers so you can react quickly in an emergency.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance when riding at night?
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distance in the dark. Keep at least three seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead when riding at night.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You can go through the intersection with caution.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must come to a complete stop and wait for a signal that lets you turn in the direction you want to go.
